## Goals

-   See rank-based tests as linear models on ranks
-   Use robust standard errors and a permutation test when assumptions fail
-   Practice choosing a model from a design

## Setup



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(marginaleffects)
```
:::



## Rank-based tests as linear models



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pg <- PlantGrowth |> rename(treatment = group)
```
:::



Kruskal-Wallis vs. a linear model on ranks:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
kruskal.test(weight ~ treatment, data = pg)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test

data:  weight by treatment
Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 7.9882, df = 2, p-value = 0.01842
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_rank <- lm(rank(weight) ~ treatment, data = pg)
anova(m_rank)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Analysis of Variance Table

Response: rank(weight)
          Df  Sum Sq Mean Sq F value  Pr(>F)  
treatment  2  618.95 309.475  5.1324 0.01291 *
Residuals 27 1628.05  60.298                  
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
```


:::
:::



The statistics are not identical, but the conclusions are close. Spearman works the same way:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
cor.test(~ Girth + Volume, data = trees, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Spearman's rank correlation rho

data:  Girth and Volume
S = 224.61, p-value < 2.2e-16
alternative hypothesis: true rho is not equal to 0
sample estimates:
      rho 
0.9547151 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
coef(lm(rank(Volume) ~ rank(Girth), data = trees))[2]
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
rank(Girth) 
   0.955004 
```


:::
:::



The Wilcoxon signed-rank test is an intercept-only model on signed ranks:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
signed_rank <- function(x) sign(x) * rank(abs(x))
d <- with(reshape(sleep, idvar = "ID", timevar = "group", direction = "wide"), extra.2 - extra.1)
wilcox.test(d, exact = FALSE)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Wilcoxon signed rank test with continuity correction

data:  d
V = 45, p-value = 0.009091
alternative hypothesis: true location is not equal to 0
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
summary(lm(signed_rank(d) ~ 1))$coefficients
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
            Estimate Std. Error  t value     Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept)      5.4     1.0105 5.343887 0.0004660833
```


:::
:::



## Unequal variances: robust standard errors

`InsectSprays` has very different variance across sprays:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(InsectSprays, aes(spray, count)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Insect counts by spray](week14-tutorial_files/figure-html/fig-sprays-1.png){#fig-sprays width=672}
:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_sp <- lm(count ~ spray, data = InsectSprays)
avg_comparisons(m_sp, variables = list(spray = "reference"))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

  Term Contrast Estimate Std. Error     z Pr(>|z|)    S   2.5 % 97.5 %
 spray    B - A    0.833        1.6  0.52    0.603  0.7  -2.305   3.97
 spray    C - A  -12.417        1.6 -7.76   <0.001 46.7 -15.555  -9.28
 spray    D - A   -9.583        1.6 -5.99   <0.001 28.8 -12.721  -6.45
 spray    E - A  -11.000        1.6 -6.87   <0.001 37.2 -14.138  -7.86
 spray    F - A    2.167        1.6  1.35    0.176  2.5  -0.971   5.30

Columns: term, contrast, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high 
Type:  response 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_comparisons(m_sp, variables = list(spray = "reference"), vcov = "HC3")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

  Term Contrast Estimate Std. Error      z Pr(>|z|)    S  2.5 % 97.5 %
 spray    B - A    0.833       1.92  0.434    0.664  0.6  -2.93   4.59
 spray    C - A  -12.417       1.54 -8.049   <0.001 50.1 -15.44  -9.39
 spray    D - A   -9.583       1.61 -5.950   <0.001 28.5 -12.74  -6.43
 spray    E - A  -11.000       1.52 -7.257   <0.001 41.2 -13.97  -8.03
 spray    F - A    2.167       2.35  0.921    0.357  1.5  -2.44   6.78

Columns: term, contrast, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::



Same estimates, different standard errors. Robust SEs trade a little power for protection when the equal-variance assumption fails.

::: callout-note
## Exercise 1

Which comparisons change the most when you switch to robust standard errors? Why do those sprays have wider or narrower intervals?
:::

## A permutation test

Is the difference between spray C and spray A larger than expected by chance?



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
two <- InsectSprays |> filter(spray %in% c("A", "C")) |> droplevels()
obs <- coef(lm(count ~ spray, data = two))[2]

set.seed(14)
perm <- replicate(5000, {
  shuffled <- two
  shuffled$spray <- sample(shuffled$spray)
  coef(lm(count ~ spray, data = shuffled))[2]
})
mean(abs(perm) >= abs(obs))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 0
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(data.frame(perm), aes(perm)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = obs, linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Permutation distribution of the difference (dashed = observed)](week14-tutorial_files/figure-html/fig-perm-1.png){#fig-perm width=672}
:::
:::
